'''Peter C. M. Molenaar''' (born 1946)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grasman |first=Raoul  |date=March 2004 |title=Stochastic maximum likelihood mean and cross-spectrum structure estimation: analytic and neuromagnetic Monte Carlo results  |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2897400|page=11}}</ref> is a Dutch developmental and mathematical psychologist who is Distinguished Professor of Human Development and Family Studies at [[Pennsylvania State University]] (Penn State).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hhd.psu.edu/molenaar-peter |title=Molenaar, Peter   |website=Penn State College of Health and Human Development |language=en |access-date=2018-07-24}}</ref> He is the [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[Multivariate Behavioral Research]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://explore.tandfonline.com/cfp/beh/multivariate-behavioral-research |title=Multivariate Behavioral Research Call for Papers 	  |website=Explore Taylor & Francis Online |language=en |access-date=2018-07-27}}</ref>

==Biography==
Molenaar received two [[bachelor's degree]]s from the [[University of Utrecht]]: one in 1972 and one in 1976. He also received two [[master's degree]]s from the University of Utrecht in 1976, one in [[mathematical psychology]] and one in [[psychophysiology]], before earning his Ph.D. in [[Social Sciences]] from the same university in 1981. He then served on the faculty of the [[University of Amsterdam]], where he eventually became head of the Department of Methodology, before joining the faculty of Penn State in 2005. In 2013, he received the Sells Award for Distinguished Multivariate Research from the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.psu.edu/story/293315/2013/10/30/academics/professor-molenaar-receives-sells-award-distinguished-mulitvariate |title=Professor Molenaar receives Sells Award for Distinguished Mulitvariate Research |date=2013-10-30 |website=Penn State News |language=en |access-date=2018-07-24}}</ref>
